v1_equilibrium.label: Conditional equilibrium scenario — not an observed market estimate
v1_equilibrium.y_axis: Price per useful-task basket index (reference scenario = 100)
v1_equilibrium.scope: One aggregate illustrative basket with quality, latency and risk constraints held fixed; neither absolute world output nor dollars
v1_equilibrium.equilibrium: If q_u<=K, (q*,p*)=(q_u,p_u). Otherwise q*=K and p*=(A/K)^(1/epsilon).
v1_equilibrium.scarcity_rent_per_unit: max(0,p*-c*(K/B)^(1/eta)) when cap binds; zero otherwise
v1_equilibrium.cost_shifter: c=(observed_fixed_basket_gpu_price_index/100)^rho; this is assumed pass-through, not estimated marginal cost. Do not combine API output price and GPU input price as independent costs.

A.meaning: Demand scale, not inferred from adopter share

epsilon.meaning: Positive absolute demand price elasticity, not estimated

K.meaning: Deliverable annual useful-task capacity relative to reference; not measured world GW

rho.meaning: Assumed pass-through of rental-price change to unit supply cost

v1_equilibrium.uncertainty: Show named sensitivity scenarios or an assumption envelope. Do not label arbitrary parameter ranges as confidence or credible intervals.
v1_equilibrium.normalization: Reference A=B=c=1 and K>=1 yields q=p=1, shown as 100. This is a unit convention, not empirical calibration.
v1_equilibrium.cost_shifter_caveat: Rental price is itself an upstream equilibrium price, not a causally exogenous supply shock. The pass-through experiment is explicitly conditional.

release_tests: The observed-price panel never uses labels global intelligence price, useful tasks measured, or measured equilibrium.
All plotted observations carry reference date, retrieval time, source and evidence class; stale snapshots remain visibly stale.
Every default quantity/capacity/elasticity scenario parameter remains labeled assumed, even when one cost input is live.
Baseline A=B=c=1,K=1.5,epsilon=eta=1 returns q=p=1.
No-cap A=B=1,epsilon=eta=1,c=0.81 returns p=0.9,q=1/0.9.
Capacity case A=4,B=c=1,epsilon=eta=1,K=1.5 returns q=1.5,p=4/1.5; price exceeds marginal cost 1.5.
Higher c weakly lowers q and weakly raises p; higher A weakly raises q and raises p; larger K never lowers q.
Reject nonfinite/nonpositive A,B,c,K,epsilon,eta and out-of-bound rho.
Do not calculate demand elasticity by regressing usage on simultaneously determined price without a valid identification design.
Missing fixed-basket items never silently drop or reweight; report coverage and stop index or label a separate matched-sample index.
Changing a canonical model version, pricing tier, geography, latency constraint or token accounting creates a new series or explicit bridge.
Batch/free/cache tiers never mix with uncached synchronous base prices.
Preserve unknown price effective dates as null; no fabricated model-age price history.
Prevent future-source/look-ahead leakage in historical backtests; only data published by historical cutoff may enter.
Do not count total data-center electricity, announced projects, training compute, GPU TDP or list inventory as deployable inference capacity.
API public access and source code license are not treated as blanket redistribution rights.
An unchanged model alias/canonical slug does not prove immutable model quality. If a service alias is used, label service-basket price only; do not claim fixed model quality.
Count default OpenRouter rows as text-output listings, never all modalities or total market size.
A provider switch must be visible and must not be silently treated as fixed-provider inflation.
Test prompt override threshold equality, UTC midnight wrap, weekday schedules and unknown condition fields; if unsupported exclude the affected entry rather than misprice it.
